description: Issue #962. The Heritage `value of … for key …` reader (`spec/grammar.md:219`'s `value-of-reader`) is ONE expression, so `spec/grammar.md:34` -- "Within a single expression, list literal, dict literal, or parenthesized group, newlines are insignificant" -- governs the slots inside it. Measured against the built parser at `e6281969`, before the fix: the bare spelling raised `ol-bad-token` twice, the list spelling three times, the dict spelling twice, and the parenthesized spelling raised `ol-bad-token` twice AND `ol-unmatched-paren` twice, on parentheses that are correctly matched -- the same phantom-diagnostic class #933 removed for arithmetic. Every claim in this paragraph was measured at that tip and re-measured after the fix. This fixture pins the CLEAN direction, which is the weaker half: the dict spelling was DIAGNOSED (those two `ol-bad-token`, describing an incomplete reader) and ALSO misread -- the tree it produced held a single entry keyed `key` whose value was a call to a procedure `k`, with the entry `a` gone -- and no diagnostic described that second half, so a fix that merely silenced the diagnostics would satisfy this file with the wrong tree still in place. `heritage/execution/heritage-value-of-key-reader-across-a-newline` therefore pins the meaning as a VALUE. `heritage-value-of-key-unmatched-paren-still-diagnosed` pins the negative direction, so removing a phantom `ol-unmatched-paren` cannot be achieved by suppressing the real one, and `heritage-value-of-key-newline-does-not-swallow-the-next-statement` pins that the continuation does not reach past the newline. The three inner slots appear twice on purpose -- once at the top level and once inside a dict entry value -- because a dictionary is the one context where a newline separates ENTRIES, so a continuation guarded by the dict-key test behaves differently there; the `for` + newline + `key` cell of exactly that cross-product was a real defect in this fix's first draft, caught in review, which is why the cross-product is pinned rather than assumed. The controls are load-bearing: the four one-line spellings were clean before the fix too, `{ a: 1` + newline + `+ 2 }` was already clean at that tip (issues #933/#956), which is what makes the failures reader-specific rather than a general expression regression, and the `key:`/`for:` dict rows pin that the tail words are still ordinary keys -- legal data, not declarations. Two passages carry that and both are cited, because reviewers twice disagreed about which one does: `spec/grammar.md:394` is the precise one for KEYWORDS ("The positions that name data ... admit keywords freely: a plain `name`, ... a `key-term`, a `dict-key` ..."), and `:410` states the property in these words ("Dictionary keys and selector bare keys are data, not declarations, so built-in names are legal keys"), which reaches `for`/`key` because `spec/built-in-names.json` lists both as `category: "keyword"` and is the authoritative list of every keyword and every primitive. The closing `print 1` / `print 2` are a weak control HERE and are labelled as such: a `check` fixture compares diagnostics only, so a reading that merged them would still be silent -- the execution twin's instruction-event count is what actually pins segmentation. One inner newline is deliberately NOT covered: between `value` and `of`, which is the reader's interception test rather than a slot inside it, and is tracked separately. Case is the third axis of that cross-product and is varied for the same reason: keywords are case-insensitive (`spec/grammar.md:13`), so an UPPERCASE or mixed-case `FOR KEY` must continue across a newline exactly as the lowercase spelling does -- a continuation comparing surface text instead of folding case would break only those rows, and every lowercase row would stay green. Measured: making either word's match case-sensitive leaves the whole Definition of Done green without these rows. No diagnostic appears on the uppercase rows, but NOT because this fixture leaves `style` off: measured, running the same source with `style: true` changes nothing. `ol-style-name-case` fires only on the reader's head `value`, which is lowercase in every row; the tail words `of`/`for`/`key` have no span of their own in the AST and are not linted at all, deferred to the #115 follow-up -- `heritage/style/name-case-uppercase-value-of-key-reader` records exactly that and is where the head's lint is pinned. The reader operates on a dict, so Heritage also needs Data (`spec/conformance.md:305`).
